posts.title: Sometimes I wonder...
posts.excerpt: What drives you to do the things you do? Automation or purpose? Joy or compulsion? All of the above?
posts.body:
I sometimes wonder why I write. Yes- I enjoy it and do I have things to say? Absolutely. But often, it isn’t for leisure or pleasure. It’s for relief. I know my brain is open- sliced by Stanley knife with the wires hanging out. My future self looms above. She’s hunched over like a mechanic; her hands covered in the residue of my shadow.

Compression is a funny thing. When your brain runs hot, it’s easy to lose track of time. Days spent in pyjama bottoms with the curtains closed, immersed in a creative process or simply just staring at the ceiling. It’s like I’m a pen, one of the ones that stained my shirt pockets as a teenager and graced every pencil case I owned. The biro that excretes deliciously fun blobs but does so in its own time. When you actually want ink it’s almost dry.

posts.title: Daydreaming- a blessing or a curse?
posts.excerpt: Having ideas is easy, but executing them? Not so much. If I had a penny for every idea I’ve had, I’d be an extremely rich woman - and probably a massive dickhead.
posts.body:
Having ideas is easy, but executing them? Not so much. If I had a penny for every idea I’ve had I’d be an extremely rich woman - and probably a massive dickhead. 

That being said, the veil between an idea and a daydream is extremely thin and in my experience? One is more addictive than the other. How often do you find yourself thinking of something awesome- about a “what if…”? Here’s one of mine:

Thought: “What if I wrote a novel that not only reflects my experiences, but articulates the absurdity of modern life and human emotion in such a way that makes people feel seen and understood?” 

Idea: “I’ll call it ‘Cross the Street.’ The main characters will live on opposite sides of a street and the road will become a metaphor for the bridges we cross to extend compassion and understanding in romance.”

But THEN, the mesh is torn. 

Daydream: “What if it actually resonates with the masses? What if it inspires empathy between men and women who seem to be pitted against each other this day and age? I know- it could be a film! I have the perfect location! Who would play me…. Emma Stone? Nah, she’s far too impressive and beautiful…”


Then, like a Tesco trolley rolled into a river, it’s abandoned. 


But it was fun while it lasted, right? You’ll definitely do it again (providing you manage to dodge Pete who seems more concerned with the reflection in his phone then ensuring Flossy and Fanny-Ann have something to push down the tinned goods aisle).

The limitless possibilities, the fantasy, the optimism- all enabled by the daydream. Because it’s much more fun to launch a trolley than it is to confront a blank page. 

By LaurenAppL 19/11/2026 


*Note: I actually did start writing “Cross the Street”- I have characters, an epilogue and a prologue. However, I was distracted by the appeal of a soundtrack and so curated a “Cross the Street” playlist. I’ll share in the comments if anyone is interested 😂.*
